channel.title: The Picky Reader — New Releases
channel.description: New and notable theology releases, tracked weekly.

item.title: The Works of Thomas Watson, 7 Volumes — Thomas Watson · gen. ed. J. Stephen Yuille
item.description: The first definitive collected edition of one of the most-quoted Puritans — now out in a definitive collected edition.

item.title: Light in the Darkness — Michael P. V. Barrett
item.description: Michael Barrett walks the whole book of Judges in 143 pages - the sin cycles, the flawed deliverers, and the faithful God behind them all. A short, redemptive-historical read from Ligonier that preaches Christ from one of the Bible's hardest books.

item.title: The Justification of the Sinless — Brendan Case
item.description: Would the Son have become incarnate had we never sinned? Case takes the old scholastic question seriously and builds a constructive Christology out of it.

item.title: Ready to Preach — Matthew D. Kim
item.description: This introductory homiletics textbook gives students and pastors a step-by-step process for crafting and communicating biblical sermons that are theologically grounded, culturally aware, and spiritually formed

item.title: Navigating Tough Texts of the Old Testament, Volume 1 — Tremper Longman III
item.description: As we read through the Bible, it's common to encounter puzzling or confusing passages. This is especially the case with the Old Testament, since its time and cultural setting are so far removed from our own. It's tempting to skip over these problem passages in our personal Bible study or in our preaching and teaching. But if all Scripture is God-breathed and useful for teaching, rebuking, correcting, and training in righteousness, those passages were preserved for our benefit.

item.title: With Me in the Valley — David Gibson
item.description: In this concise booklet, David Gibson examines the believer's union with Christ as the sheep and the shepherd depicted in Psalm 23, offering readers comfort in the hope of trusting him.

item.title: Persuasive Preaching — David R. Helm & Jeremy Meeks
item.description: This 9Marks book offers practical tips on public speaking that pastors can apply in their sermons to bring clarity, spark interest, and demonstrate care for their audiences.

item.title: God's Presence with Us and in Us: A Biblical Theology of the Holy Spirit — Miguel Echevarría · ESBT series
item.description: A whole-Bible study of the Spirit's presence, tracing the theme from Eden to the new creation.

item.title: Why We Worship: Experiencing Heaven on Earth at Church — Adriel Sanchez
item.description: A pastoral case for gathered worship as a foretaste of heaven.

item.title: Reformation and Tradition — Joshua Benjamins
item.description: Does the Reformation stand against the church’s ancient tradition, or grow out of it? These collected essays take up the legacy of Nicene theology and make the case that the Reformers were heirs of the early church’s creedal confession rather than its critics—a thoughtful entry in the renewed conversation over what Nicaea still means for Protestant faith.

item.title: A Path for Cultural Analysis — Vern Poythress
item.description: To understand our world, we don’t need more secular theories; we need more Scripture. In A Path for Cultural Analysis, Vern S. Poythress replaces broken modern frameworks with a distinctly biblical roadmap for the twenty-first century.

item.title: Talk About What Matters Most — J. Alasdair Groves
item.description: Practical help for men to move past isolation and build real, honest friendships.

item.title: Directive Biblical Counseling — Jonathan Moorhead
item.description: A six-session framework for counseling from Scripture, designed for both self-counsel and helping others in the local church. Out now. Practical, confessional, and short enough to hand to a small group leader.

item.title: Shepherding Time — Rush Witt & Joe Keller
item.description: Time management for pastors framed as stewardship and worship rather than productivity. Short, practical, and free of the usual hustle.

item.title: Apocryphal Gospels — Gregory R. Lanier
item.description: Lanier sorts the noncanonical gospels from the four the church actually received - what they are, when they were written, and why they keep getting deployed against the canon. Apologetics done with the primary sources in hand rather than around them.

item.title: Faith and Freedom — Eric Patterson and Jennifer Marshall Patterson
item.description: Six essays making the case for religious liberty as a Christian conviction rather than a political convenience. Short enough to hand to a deacon board, serious enough to hold up under one.

item.title: Nary a Horse Left Standing — Lee Alan Dugatkin
item.description: How a devastating outbreak of horse flu in the 1870s ground city life to a halt - but ultimately revolutionized animal rights, medicine, and transportation.

item.title: The Cross in Context — Christopher Woznicki
item.description: A study of the atonement in its biblical and theological context.

item.title: The Cathedral of Theology: Principles of Christian Dogmatics — J. V. Fesko
item.description: A major new systematic-theology framework from a leading Reformed dogmatician — one of the season's most anticipated academic releases.

item.title: The Spirit-Led Family — Marty Machowski
item.description: Marty Machowski on the Holy Spirit's work in the home - pneumatology for parents who want their children to know God's presence, not just his rules. Family discipleship with real theology under it.

item.title: The AI Apocalypse — Collin Hansen
item.description: The AI Apocalypse brings together an international and interdisciplinary group of contributors from across the fields of technology, theology, and ethics. They’ll help you navigate our new AI world with wisdom and clarity. And they’ll show you how the living message of Christ provides a more stable foundation than AI’s promises.

item.title: Partnership with Priority — John Sypert
item.description: Drawing deeply from Spurgeon's sermons, institutions, and vast ministry output, this book reveals a missiology that is both compassionate and convictional.

item.title: The Worship of the Reformed Church — Terry L. Johnson
item.description: A comprehensive case for recovering the biblical, theological, and historical foundations of historic Reformed worship.

item.title: The Victory Mine — J. Stephen Yuille
item.description: The fourth volume in Stephen Yuille's Puritan daily-reading series: ninety days of a Puritan quotation, a Scripture, and a pastoral reflection. The easiest on-ramp into the Puritans there is, in a handsome hardcover.

item.title: The Call to Contextualize — Jae Hoon Lee
item.description: Twenty years of ministry at Seoul's Onnuri Church behind a book on communicating the gospel across genuine difference. Contextualization argued by a practitioner rather than a theorist.

item.title: Archaeology and the Revelation of John — David A. deSilva
item.description: deSilva walks the seven cities with a camera, and more than 250 photographs put Revelation back in the world it was written to. Reference and gift book at once.

item.title: Theology for Life — Ronni Kurtz
item.description: A first systematic theology for readers who have never opened one, presenting doctrine as something to enjoy rather than survive. Kurtz writes from the Baptist academy but aims squarely at the pew.

item.title: An Introduction to Reformed Apologetics — J. V. Fesko
item.description: In An Introduction to Reformed Apologetics, J. V. Fesko gives readers the foundational tools they need to defend the Christian faith. Drawing from Paul's example in Acts and the legacy of great apologists throughout church history, Fesko presents twelve guiding theses for Christian apologetics.

item.title: Future Grace — John Piper
item.description: In Future Grace, John Piper offers meditations grounded in solid biblical reflection, helping readers defeat the power of sin by banking on the promises of Christ.

item.title: Talking to Kids about Hard Things — Rebekah Hannah & Michael Keller
item.description: Rebekah Hannah and Michael Keller, with a foreword from Kathy Keller, on gospel-centered conversations with kids about identity, doubt, suffering, and cultural pressure. A parenting book that trusts children with the truth.
